Education

  • Ph.D. in Mass Communication, Loughborough University, UK (2018)
  • M.A. in Journalism, National Taiwan University, Taiwan (2008)

Experiences

  • Associate Professor, Graduate Institute of Journalism, National Taiwan University (2024.8–present)
  • Assistant Professor, Graduate Institute of Journalism, National Taiwan University (2022.8–2024.7)
  • Project-Appointed Assistant Professor, Department of Adult and Continuing Education, National Taiwan Normal University (2021.8–2022.7)
  • Assistant Professor, Department of Mass Communication, Tamkang University (2018.8–2021.7)

Journal Articles

  • Meng, J., Tsai, H. J., & Lin, Y. P. (2026). From records to actions: mediating civic data and environmental activism in Taiwan. Information, Communication & Society, 1–20. https://doi.org/10.1080/1369118X.2026.2686318
  • Meng, J., Lin, Y.-P., & Tsai, H.-J. (2024). Environmental activism in the platform society: Spatial agency in digital maps. New Media & Society, 26(12), 7058–7080.
  • Tsai, H.-J. (2023). Data activism: Initiatives, practices, and connections among NGO workers and open-source communities in a platformized civil society. Communication and Society, 64, 29–62. [In Chinese]
  • Tsai, H.-J. (2022). Platform capitalism: Spectacle and crisis of platformized cultural industries. Taiwan: A Radical Quarterly in Social Studies, 121, 209–217. [In Chinese]
  • Tsai, H.-J., & Lin, Y.-P. (2021). Precarious media labor in the era of post-COVID-19: Rethinking the supporting policy for the film and TV industry globally and in Taiwan. Mass Communication Research, 148, 1–46. [In Chinese]
  • Tsai, H. (2021). Contextualizing the phenomenon of Big Data: A looming crisis of monopolies in the global media & Big Tech. Taiwan Journal of East Asian Studies, 18(1), 89–130. [In Chinese]
  • Tsai, H. (2020). Audience commodity in the age of streaming services: An analysis of Netflix binge-watching and the associated audience labor through critical political economy of communications. Chinese Journal of Communication Research, 37, 83–112. [In Chinese]

Book Chapters

  • Tsai, H. (2022). Critical visual literacy in the digital media era. In W.-C. Wang, Y.-P. Lin & L.-J. Wang (Eds.), Digital Communication Literacy Education in the AI Era (pp. 233–255). Wunan, Taipei.
  • Tsai, H. (2021). Towards critical data research: Rethinking information and platform monopolies. In C.-D. Liu & C.-S. Feng (Eds.), Communication is Understanding: A Critical Analysis of Contemporary Cross-Strait Media Issues (pp. 233–255). Taipei: NCCU COM Research & Development Center.
  • Lin, Y.-P., & Tsai, H.-J. (2020). Indie music as cool ambassadors? The international dimension of music policy in Taiwan, 2010–2017. In E. Tsai, T. Ho & M. Jian (Eds.), Made in Taiwan: Studies in Popular Music (pp. 171–188). Routledge.
  • Tsai, H.-J., & Lin, Y.-P. (2018). Neoliberalised development of cultural policies in Taiwan and a case of the Taiwanese film industry in a creative industries model. In V. Durrer, T. Miller & D. O'Brien (Eds.), The Routledge Handbook of Global Cultural Policy (pp. 449–467). London: Routledge.
  • Tsai, H. (2016). Fighting the neoliberalised media market & state interference: The interdependency of the Taiwan PTS and civil society organisations. In Lowe & Yamamoto (Eds.), Public Service Media Across Borders and Boundaries, RIPE@2015 (pp. 121–135). Goteborg: Nordicom.

Conference Papers

  • Tsai, H.-J. (2025, June). Contesting visibility: Taiwanese independent media's strategies under platformised audience metrics. Island Voices on the Move: Sinophone Research Forum – Taiwan Workshop, University of Leeds, UK.
  • Tsai, H.-J. (2024, September). Alternative pathways: Taiwanese independent media's strategies against platform logic. ANCHOR / ANGER AWEIGHT: Cultural Typhoon 2024, Japan.
  • Meng, J., Lin, Y.-P., & Tsai, H.-J. (2023, July). App activism and negotiated politics in the digital age: Towards a typology. IAMCR 2023, Lyon, France.
  • Tsai, H.-J., & Lin, Y.-P. (2022, May). Data activism in Taiwan: The practice and connection of NGO workers and open source communities in a platformized civil society. 72nd ICA Annual Conference, Paris, France.
  • Lin, Y.-P., & Tsai, H.-J. (2021, September). New challenges of public service media in a streaming era: The case of PTS+ in Taiwan. RIPE@2021, Online Conference, Fribourg, Switzerland.
  • Tsai, H.-J., & Lin, Y.-P. (2021, March). Neoliberalised cultural policy-making: The case of music-export policy in Taiwan since 2010. ICCPR 2020, Online Conference, Kyoto, Japan.
  • Tsai, H.-J., & Lin, Y.-P. (2019, December). How does public service media survive the competition from new streaming services? The case of PTS+ in Taiwan. Subscription Video-on-Demand in East Asia Conference, Ritsumeikan University, Kyoto, Japan.
  • Lin, Y.-P., & Tsai, H.-J. (2019, July). How Facebook transformed news production and distribution: An examination of news media organizations and social media curators in Taiwan. IAMCR 2019, Madrid, Spain.
  • Lin, Y.-P., & Tsai, H.-J. (2019, May). National funding for supporting indie music? How Taiwanese government promotes music industry globally, 2011–2017. 69th ICA Annual Conference, Washington D.C., USA.
  • Tsai, H.-J. (2017, August). After the neoliberal reform: Creative industries in Taiwan. 13th Conference of the European Sociological Association, Athens, Greece.
  • Tsai, H.-J. (2016, November). The rapid and continuing expansion of the creative industries sector in Taiwan. ECREA 6th European Communication Conference, Prague, Czech Republic.
  • Tsai, H.-J. (2016, July). Neoliberal legislation of creative industries policy in Taiwan. International Conference on Cultural Policy Research 2016, Seoul, Korea.

Awards and Honors

  • Excellence in Teaching Award, Tamkang University (2020)
  • Chiang Ching-kuo Foundation for International Scholarly Exchange (2017–2018)
  • Santander Mobility Award, Loughborough University (2016)
  • John Guest Phillips Memorial Travelling Scholarship, Loughborough University (2015)
  • Santander Funding for Travel Awards and Research Collaboration, Loughborough University (2014)
  • Government Scholarships for Overseas Study (GSOS), Ministry of Education, Taiwan (2013–2016)

Research Interests

  • New Media & Civic Engagement
  • Platformisation of Communication
  • Public Service Media
  • Democratisation of Mass Culture

External Links
